item_title: Tech companies like Google and Microsoft have offered a muted response to unrest in Iran, prompting side projects by employees to fight censorship and more
item_description: Paresh Dave / Wired:  — Companies like Google have offered a muted response to unrest in Iran. Grassroots coders are tackling internet censorship on their own.

item_title: Google cuts most of the Area 120 team and will graduate three of the incubator's projects in 2023; sources: staff not involved in those projects were laid off
item_description: Julia Love / Bloomberg:  — Alphabet Inc.'s Google has cut most of the jobs at Area 120, its in-house incubator for new projects, as part of a broad wave of layoffs across the company.

item_title: Emails and sources: Google fired 16% of its ~400-person Fuchsia OS team, Research cut jobs in low traction areas, and Cloud cut operational and other roles
item_description: New York Times:  — The layoffs amount to about 6 percent of the global work force at the company, the latest tech giant to make cuts after a pandemic hiring spree.

item_title: Internal records: Twitter now has around 1,300 active employees, including fewer than 550 full-time engineers, and about 1,400 non-working employees
item_description: Lora Kolodny / CNBC:  — - Internal records show that Twitter has shed about 80% of its employees since Elon Musk took over and headcount is hovering around 1,300 employees today.

item_title: How Dutch privacy negotiators, empowered by GDPR, have spurred major changes at Google, Microsoft, Zoom, and others, as the Netherlands punches above its weight
item_description: Natasha Singer / New York Times:  — Dutch privacy negotiators have spurred major changes at Google, Microsoft and Zoom, using a landmark European data protection law as a lever.
